title: Where the energy goes in a pulley system
examples: Why is a real pulley system less than perfect?
Can a machine give out more energy than you put in?

explain.say: Pulleys, levers and gears let a small force move a big load, but they never give out more energy than you put in. Here is where the energy goes in a typical small block and tackle.

draw.text: Where the energy goes in a pulley system

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: pulleys. Look at the fixed pulley, the movable pulley and the rope. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Where the energy goes in a pulley system

explain.say: Most of the work you do, around 80 percent here, goes into raising the load. That is the useful part.
Some is lost to friction: the wheels rub on their axles and the rope bends round the wheels. That energy warms the parts slightly.
A little goes into lifting the bottom block itself, which rises with the load. Efficiency is useful energy out divided by energy in: 80 percent here, and always less than 100 percent.

faq.q: Can a machine give out more energy than you put in?
faq.a: No. Energy cannot be created. A machine can multiply force, but then you move further, and some energy is always lost, so the useful energy out is less than the energy in.

faq.q: Where does the lost energy go?
faq.a: Mostly into heat from friction in the wheel axles and the rope bending, plus lifting the moving block. It spreads out into the surroundings and is not useful.

faq.q: Why is friction in pulleys a problem?
faq.a: Friction turns some of your work into heat instead of lifting. More wheels give more mechanical advantage but also more friction, so very large pulley systems become less efficient.
asks: How can I reduce friction in pulleys?

faq.a: Efficiency is the useful energy out divided by the total energy in, often given as a percentage. A pulley system that uses 80 joules of every 100 to lift the load is 80 percent efficient.
asks: How do you work out efficiency?

faq.q: How can a machine be made more efficient?
faq.a: Use ball bearings in the wheels, oil moving parts, lighter blocks and flexible rope. These cut friction and wasted lifting.

facts: Efficiency equals useful energy output divided by total energy input.
No machine can be more than 100 percent efficient.

quiz.say: You do 500 J of work and the load gains 400 J. What is the efficiency?
quiz.show: You do 500 J of work and the load gains 400 J. What is the efficiency?
quiz.why: 400 divided by 500 is 0.8, which is 80 percent.

wrong.1: That divides the wrong way; efficiency is never above 100 percent.
wrong.2: Some energy is lost to friction, so it cannot be 100 percent.
